title: DatGold hooks.json
description: Lifecycle hooks for the DatGold Hub: the documented subset of the Claude Code hooks schema. The owner's file is <Hub data folder>/hooks.json; a project may ship .chatmcp/hooks.json, which is ignored until the owner approves its sha256. The Hub validates in code (lib/hooks.mjs); tests/verify-hooks-core.mjs checks that this file and the loader accept and refuse the same configurations.

hooks.description: Event name -> matcher groups. PreToolUse, PostToolUse and PostToolUseFailure fire for every tool call; Stop, TaskCompleted and SubagentStop are accepted and run by the hooks runner but are wired to the agent loop in a later release. Every other Claude Code event name is accepted and ignored (the loader warns).

matcher.description: Tested against the tool name of the tool events. Empty, "*" or absent: every tool. Only letters, digits, _ - space , and |: an exact name or a list of exact names. Anything else is an unanchored JavaScript regular expression. A DatGold name (local.run_command) and the Claude Code name (Bash) both match; an external tool answers to mcp__server__tool. Ignored by Stop, TaskCompleted and SubagentStop.

commandHandler.description: The only handler type this build runs. Exec form (args present): command is the program, started without a shell. Shell form (no args): command is a script for bash, powershell or cmd. Exit 0: stdout is read as one JSON object. Exit 2: blocks (PreToolUse, Stop, TaskCompleted, SubagentStop) with stderr as the reason; on the Post events it is feedback to the model. Any other exit code does not block unless onFailure is block (on Stop, SubagentStop and TaskCompleted onFailure has no effect: only exit 2 or a block decision holds the agent back).

timeout.description: Seconds. Default 600 (the Claude Code default). The process and everything it started are killed when the time is up.

onFailure.description: block: a non-zero exit other than 2, a timeout or a program that cannot be started blocks the action. continue (default): it does not. No effect on Stop, SubagentStop and TaskCompleted: a failure there is logged and never blocks.

if.description: One permission-rule style condition, for example Bash(git *) or Edit(src/**). Only for the tool events. A condition that cannot be evaluated lets the hook run.

async.description: Accepted for compatibility; this build runs the hook synchronously.

asyncRewake.description: Accepted for compatibility; this build runs the hook synchronously.

once.description: Accepted for compatibility; only skill frontmatter honours it in Claude Code.
